title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 104
paragraphs: This Miltiades, then, at the time of which I speak, had come from the Chersonese and was now a general of the Athenians, having escaped death in two different forms. The Phoenicians, pursuing him as far as Imbros, had done everything they could to capture him and bring him before the king. After he escaped them and returned to his own country, and seemed at last to be safe, his enemies, who had been lying in wait for him at home, prosecuted him in court for his tyranny in the Chersonese. Having escaped their efforts too, he was elected by the people and appointed a general of the Athenians.
